notes: Cats: the subject is Certified only and the Régionale bank has no category for it, so intro is empty; Southern France in the Village bank carries Provence and the Languedoc. The Southwest and Dordogne stems sit under Sweet Wines (Jurançon, Pacherenc, Monbazillac, Saussignac) and the Banyuls and Rivesaltes stems under Fortified Wines, both left out because those categories carry Sauternes, Tokaji, Port and Sherry as well; they are counted in the review. Chapters: no Régionale chapter covers the south; the Village chapter Southern France runs Provence, the Languedoc, Roussillon and the Southwest with Cahors, Madiran, Jurançon, Bergerac and Monbazillac. Regions: provence and languedoc-roussillon, the two articles the join hangs on the category; there is no Southwest article. Country: france for the climate card and the Vin Doux Naturel card. Grapes: the Court's named varieties whose profile carries the south, in their Village form where two exist: the Mediterranean five for Provence and the Languedoc, Vermentino for the Court's Rolle, Muscat Blanc for Muscat de Rivesaltes, Malbec for Cahors, Tannat for Madiran, Petit Manseng for Jurançon; Clairette, Ugni Blanc, Mauzac and Gros Manseng have no profile, and the international grapes of the Languedoc and Bergerac are left to their own subjects. Techniques: vin doux naturel for mutage, rosé methods for Provence, noble rot for Monbazillac, the traditional method for Crémant de Limoux. No service table: the Court sets no service row for the south.
